sentences.en: Imagine volunteering to live on Mars for 378 days.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，自愿在火星上生活378天。

sentences.en: Only you never actually leave planet Earth.
sentences.zh: 只是你从未真正离开过地球。

sentences.en: You walk through a plain white office door inside of a warehouse in Houston.
sentences.zh: 你走进休斯顿一个仓库里的一扇普通白色办公室门。

sentences.en: The door shuts behind you.
sentences.zh: 门在你身后关上了。

sentences.en: And you're locked inside a stage designed to look like a Martian habitat.
sentences.zh: 你被锁在一个看起来像火星栖息地的舞台里。

sentences.en: For more than a year, you and three other volunteers are completely isolated from the outside world inside this 1,700 square foot structure
sentences.zh: 一年多来，你和其他三名志愿者在这个1,700平方英尺的结构中与外界完全隔绝，

sentences.en: where everything is made from 3D printed imitation Martian rock.
sentences.zh: 这里的一切都是用3D打印的仿火星岩石制成的。

sentences.en: You eat freeze-dried space food for every meal.
sentences.zh: 你每一顿饭都吃冷冻干燥的太空食品。

sentences.en: You wear virtual reality goggles and walk around a red sandbox to simulate spacewalks.
sentences.zh: 你戴着虚拟现实护目镜，在红色的沙箱里走来走去，模拟太空行走。

sentences.en: You're under near-constant surveillance from mission control.
sentences.zh: 你处于任务控制中心近乎持续的监视之下。

sentences.en: And to mimic the actual conditions of communication between Earth and Mars, any message you send to family or friends back home takes at least 22 minutes to arrive.
sentences.zh: 为了模拟地球和火星之间真实的通信条件，你发给家人或朋友的任何信息至少需要22分钟才能到达。

sentences.en: To the people who applied, mainly NASA superfans who were required to have master's degrees in math or science, this experiment sounded like a dream come true.
sentences.zh: 对于那些申请者来说，主要是拥有数学或科学硕士学位的NASA超级粉丝，这个实验听起来就像梦想成真。

sentences.en: The chance to make a noble sacrifice for the future of humanity.
sentences.zh: 这是为人类未来做出崇高牺牲的机会。

sentences.en: Being invited to participate felt like winning a tour of Willy Wonka's chocolate factory, even though we know, through repeated research over many decades,
sentences.zh: 受邀参加感觉就像赢得了参观威利·旺卡巧克力工厂的机会，尽管我们通过几十年来反复的研究知道，

sentences.en: the pernicious effects of prolonged, confined isolation on the human psyche.
sentences.zh: 长期封闭隔离对人类心理的有害影响。

sentences.en: The study is in progress right now, and it's coming to an end this summer.
sentences.zh: 这项研究目前正在进行中，将于今年夏天结束。

sentences.en: What will NASA learn from this that we don't already know?
sentences.zh: NASA能从中了解到我们还不知道的什么呢？

sentences.en: And when the participants leave that stage set, how will they have changed?
sentences.zh: 当参与者离开那个舞台布景时，他们会发生怎样的改变？

sentences.en: I'm Nathaniel Rich, and I'm a contributor to the New York Times magazine based in New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 我是纳撒尼尔·里奇，我是常驻新奥尔良的《纽约时报》杂志撰稿人。

sentences.en: I tend to be drawn to stories that have environmental themes with moral dimensions that lack clear solutions.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于被那些具有道德维度且缺乏明确解决方案的环境主题故事所吸引。

sentences.en: This week's Sunday Read is a piece I wrote for the magazine about CHAPIA, this bizarre experiment being conducted by NASA's Mars Research Division.
sentences.zh: 本周的《周日阅读》是我为该杂志写的一篇关于CHAPIA的文章，这是NASA火星研究部门正在进行的奇怪实验。

sentences.en: NASA claims it wants to determine the effects of prolonged isolation on astronauts chosen to serve on the first human mission to Mars, or on future Mars colonists.
sentences.zh: NASA声称它想确定长期隔离对被选中执行首次载人火星任务的宇航员或未来火星殖民者的影响。

sentences.en: I came to this story through my own pet obsession with isolation experiments.
sentences.zh: 我通过自己对隔离实验的痴迷接触到了这个故事。

sentences.en: I've been fascinated by a couple of studies from a few decades ago, including a series of tests where people were imprisoned in subterranean caves
sentences.zh: 几十年来，我一直对几项研究着迷，包括一系列将人们关在地下洞穴中的测试，

sentences.en: for long periods of time to see what would happen to them, to their sense of reality, their sleep schedules, and their brains.
sentences.zh: 持续很长一段时间，看看他们会发生什么，看看他们的现实感、睡眠时间表和大脑会发生什么。

sentences.en: The stories of some of these experiments end in spectacular tragedy.
sentences.zh: 其中一些实验的故事以惊人的悲剧告终。

sentences.en: I was curious to know whether anyone was still conducting major isolation tests today.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇今天是否还有人在进行重大的隔离测试。

sentences.en: As it turns out, NASA has been conducting isolation experiments for decades in preparation for the colonization of the moon and other planets,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，为了准备殖民月球和其他行星，NASA几十年来一直在进行隔离实验，

sentences.en: to see whether people living in outer space would go mad.
sentences.zh: 看看生活在外太空的人是否会发疯。

sentences.en: As I started to look into this current study, it raised a lot of larger questions, not just about isolation, but about space exploration,
sentences.zh: 当我开始研究这项当前的研究时，它引发了许多更大的问题，不仅是关于隔离，还有关于太空探索，

sentences.en: and about humanity's relationship with our own planet.
sentences.zh: 以及人类与我们自己星球的关系。

sentences.en: There's a certain element of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国太空计划中有一种非常胜利主义和轻浮的元素，

sentences.en: space program that's very triumphalist and giddy, the excitement of discovering new worlds.
sentences.zh: 即发现新世界的兴奋感。

sentences.en: But there's also a mournful quality to our dreams of space colonization.
sentences.zh: 但我们对太空殖民的梦想中也有一种悲伤的特质。

sentences.en: Think of the familiar image from science fiction of the astronaut trapped in a spacesuit, floating off into the oblivion of outer space.
sentences.zh: 想想科幻小说中那个被困在宇航服里，漂浮在茫茫外太空中的宇航员的熟悉形象。

sentences.en: That mournfulness, even that sense of horror, seems to mirror the tone of these isolation experiments.
sentences.zh: 那种悲伤，甚至那种恐惧感，似乎反映了这些隔离实验的基调。

sentences.en: The idea of locking yourself up willingly to figure out what'll happen to you when pushed beyond what's conventionally thought to be healthy or humane.
sentences.zh: 为了弄清楚当你被推向超出通常认为健康或人道的范围时会发生什么，而自愿把自己锁起来的想法。

sentences.en: I spoke with Jeffrey Mathias, a science historian at Cornell University, who's writing a book about the history of isolation research.
sentences.zh: 我采访了康奈尔大学的科学史学家杰弗里·马蒂亚斯，他正在写一本关于隔离研究历史的书。

sentences.en: I asked him, why do we keep doing this research over and over again when we already know what isolation does to people?
sentences.zh: 我问他，既然我们已经知道隔离对人有什么影响，为什么我们还要一遍又一遍地做这项研究？

sentences.en: And he said, it's not actually about what we're going to find out.
sentences.zh: 他说，这实际上不是关于我们将要发现什么。

sentences.en: It's about satisfying an urge.
sentences.zh: 这是关于满足一种冲动。

sentences.en: He likened the Mars experiments to a traumatic repetition.
sentences.zh: 他将火星实验比作一种创伤性重复。

sentences.en: He told me, we're coming to terms with the trauma of having ruined this planet.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，我们正在接受毁掉这个星球的创伤。

sentences.en: And we're trying to enact some kind of utopian future where we don't make the same mistakes again.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图制定某种乌托邦式的未来，在那里我们不会再犯同样的错误。

sentences.en: So here's my story.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事。

sentences.en: Can humans endure the psychological torment of Mars?
sentences.zh: 人类能忍受火星的心理折磨吗？

sentences.zh: 艾丽莎·香农当时正从奥克兰通勤到萨克拉门托，她在那里的一所大学医院担任高级执业护士。

sentences.en: When NASA called to tell her that she had been selected for a Mars mission, she screamed and pulled off the highway.
sentences.zh: 当NASA打电话告诉她她被选中执行火星任务时，她尖叫着把车开出了高速公路。

sentences.en: As soon as she hung up, she called her partner, an information security operations manager at the University of California, Berkeley, named Jake Harwood.
sentences.zh: 挂断电话后，她立即给她的伴侣打了电话，他是加州大学伯克利分校的信息安全运营经理，名叫杰克·哈伍德。

sentences.en: Wow, Harwood said.
sentences.zh: “哇，”哈伍德说。

sentences.en: Yeah, Shannon said.
sentences.zh: “是的，”香农说。

sentences.en: Wow.
They sat in silence with the information, struggling to fathom the shape and weight of it for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 他们带着这个消息沉默地坐着，很长一段时间里都在努力去理解它的形状和分量。

sentences.en: Later that morning, Nathan Jones, an emergency room physician in Springfield, Illinois, received the call that he had so fervently awaited and so deeply dreaded.
sentences.zh: 那天晚些时候，伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德的急诊室医生内森·琼斯接到了他热切期待又深感恐惧的电话。

sentences.en: His thoughts turned immediately to his wife, Casey, and their three sons, who were 8, 10, and 12.
sentences.zh: 他的思绪立刻转向了他的妻子凯西和他们三个分别为8岁、10岁和12岁的儿子。

sentences.en: You get only 18 years with your kids, he told himself.
sentences.zh: “你和孩子在一起的时间只有18年，”他对自己说。

sentences.en: If you accept this opportunity, you'll have to give up one of them.
sentences.zh: “如果你接受这个机会，你将不得不放弃其中一年。”

sentences.en: And yet, he couldn't possibly turn down NASA.
sentences.zh: 然而，他不可能拒绝NASA。

sentences.en: Mars, he had convinced himself, was his destiny.
sentences.zh: 他确信，火星是他的命运。

sentences.en: As a child, he dreamed of walking across an alien planet in a state of wonder.
sentences.zh: 小时候，他梦想着在惊叹中走过一颗外星行星。

sentences.en: He hoped to attend space camp, but his family couldn't afford it.
sentences.zh: 他希望能参加太空营，但他的家庭负担不起。

sentences.en: Once his sons were old enough, he took them to Cape Canaveral for a rocket launch.
sentences.zh: 当他的儿子们长大后，他带他们去卡纳维拉尔角观看火箭发射。

sentences.en: When he told Casey the news, she nearly burst into tears.
sentences.zh: 当他把这个消息告诉凯西时，她差点泪流满面。

sentences.en: This Mars mission,
sentences.zh: 这次火星任务，

sentences.en: CHAPIA, would not actually go to Mars, but the success of CHAPIA,
sentences.zh: CHAPIA，实际上并不会去火星，但CHAPIA的成功，

sentences.en: Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog, will hang on the precision with which it simulates the first human expedition to Mars,
sentences.zh: 即“乘员健康与性能探索模拟”，将取决于它模拟首次载人火星探险的精确程度，

sentences.en: an eventuality that NASA expects to occur by 2040.
sentences.zh: 这是NASA预计到2040年将会发生的事情。

sentences.en: That people will travel to Mars, and soon, is a widely accepted conviction within NASA.
sentences.zh: 人类将前往火星，而且很快，这是NASA内部广泛接受的信念。

sentences.en: The target date for the initial human mission has drifted slightly.
sentences.zh: 首次载人任务的目标日期已经略有推迟。

sentences.en: In a 2018 report commissioned by Congress,
sentences.zh: 在国会委托的一份2018年报告中，

sentences.en: NASA estimated that the first human beings would land on Mars no later than the late 2020s, but the certainty has not wavered, even if technical hurdles remain.
sentences.zh: NASA估计第一批人类将在2020年代末之前登陆火星，但即使技术障碍依然存在，这种确定性并没有动摇。

sentences.en: Rachel McCauley, until recently the acting deputy director of NASA's Mars campaign, had, as of July, a punch list of 800 problems that must be solved
sentences.zh: 直到最近还是NASA火星计划代理副主任的雷切尔·麦考利，截至7月，有一份必须解决的800个问题的清单，

sentences.en: before the first human mission launches.
sentences.zh: 在首次载人任务发射之前。

sentences.en: Many of these concern the mechanical difficulties of transporting people to a planet that is never closer than 33.9 million miles away, keeping them alive on poisonous soil
sentences.zh: 其中许多涉及将人类运送到距离从未小于3390万英里的行星上的机械困难，让他们在有毒的土壤上生存，

sentences.en: in unbreathable air, bombarded by solar radiation and galactic cosmic rays without access to immediate communication, and returning them safely to Earth,
sentences.zh: 在无法呼吸的空气中，受到太阳辐射和银河宇宙射线的轰击，无法进行即时通信，并在一年半后安全返回地球，

sentences.en: more than a year and a half later.
sentences.zh: 这些都是问题。

sentences.en: Many other problems involve technical details so arcane that
sentences.zh: 许多其他问题涉及的技术细节非常深奥，以至于

sentences.en: Macaulay wouldn't even know how to begin explaining them to a well-intentioned journalist lacking an advanced engineering degree.
sentences.zh: 麦考利甚至不知道如何向一位没有高级工程学位的善意记者解释。

sentences.en: But Macaulay does not doubt that NASA will overcome these challenges.
sentences.zh: 但麦考利并不怀疑NASA会克服这些挑战。

sentences.en: What NASA does not yet know, what nobody can know, is whether humanity can overcome the psychological torment of Martian life.
sentences.zh: NASA尚不知道的是，没有人能知道的是，人类是否能克服火星生活的心理折磨。

sentences.en: Enter Chupia.
sentences.zh: 进入Chupia。

sentences.en: Instead of asking questions about aeroshell sensor design and terrain-relative navigation, it promised to ask questions about people.
sentences.zh: 它承诺不再问关于气动外壳传感器设计和地形相对导航的问题，而是问关于人的问题。

sentences.en: For 378 days, four ordinary people would enact, as closely as possible, the lives of Martian colonists, receiving directives, feedback, and near-total surveillance
sentences.zh: 在378天的时间里，四名普通人将尽可能真实地演绎火星殖民者的生活，接收来自任务控制中心的指令、反馈和近乎全面的监视。

sentences.en: from mission control.
sentences.zh: 他们将吃宇航员食品，进行基础实验，执行维护职责，回答无休止的调查，并享受高度结构化的休息时间。

sentences.en: They would eat astronaut food, conduct basic experiments, perform maintenance duties, respond to endless surveys, and enjoy highly structured downtime.
sentences.zh: 这种极端的逼真程度对于确保实验准确确定人类在远离他们所认识的每个人的数百万英里之外生活时是否能茁壮成长是必要的。

sentences.en: This level of extreme verisimilitude is necessary to ensure that the experiment accurately determines whether human beings can thrive while living millions of miles
sentences.zh: 实验者想了解机组人员是否可以在数百天内食用低盐、预包装的宇航员餐而不失去食欲、体重和积极态度，他们是否可以在封闭空间内与陌生人和谐相处，他们是否可以在与地球失去联系长达三周的情况下保持一个有凝聚力的专业环境。

sentences.en: from everybody they've ever known.
sentences.zh: 这些问题至关重要，因为如果居住者不能保持健康、快乐，最重要的是，

sentences.en: Experimenters wanted to learn whether crew members could eat low-salt, pre-packaged astronaut meals for hundreds of days without losing their appetite, weight,
sentences.zh: 他们的理智，那么任何火星任务都无法成功。

sentences.en: and positive attitude, whether they could live in harmony with strangers in a confined space, whether they could preserve a cohesive, professional environment
sentences.zh: 因此，在NASA能够安全判断宇航员是否会在火星上茁壮成长之前，

sentences.en: when they are out of contact with Earth for as long as three weeks at a time.
sentences.zh: NASA必须首先确定宇航员模仿者是否能在设计得尽可能像火星的舞台布景上茁壮成长。

sentences.en: Such questions are of paramount importance because no mission to Mars can succeed if its inhabitants cannot maintain their health, their happiness, and, most critical of all,

sentences.en: their sanity.
sentences.zh: 与大多数NASA任务不同，
